result:
**Verification of the common part (a):** Solutions 1 and 3 agree on a = u(1 − d/v), and I can confirm it.

- E[L(t)] = ∫₀ᵗ ∫ p¹ₛ p²ₛ dμ ds ≍ ∫₀ᵗ s^{−d/v} ds, which is finite iff d/v < 1. So the inverse collision local time is a stable subordinator of index β = 1 − d/v.
- Since u ≤ v, the slower process X¹ (walk dimension u) sets the time scale for a ball of radius r, so ν(B(x,r)) ≍ L(r^u) ≍ r^{u(1−d/v)}.
- Cross-check with the two-point kernel: G(r) = ∫ p¹ₜ p²ₜ dt ≍ r^{−(d + ud/v − u)}. This is singular exactly when d/u + d/v > 1, which is the stated condition. The energy/Frostman exponent is d − (d + ud/v − u) = u(1 − d/v), which matches.

Solution 2 has a = u − d, which contradicts this computation, so it is wrong.

**Logarithmic factors:**

- The Taylor–Wendel exact gauge for a β-stable regenerative set is h(t) = t^β (log log(1/t))^{1−β}. Substituting t = r^u gives log log(1/t) ≍ log log(1/r), so c = 1 − β = d/v and b = 0.
- The condition d/u + d/v > 1 is what makes G a pure power, with no logarithm. A logarithmic factor would only appear at the boundary d/u + d/v = 1, so there is no evident source for the nonzero b = d/u + d/v − 1 in Solution 3.
- Solution 3's c = 1 − (u/d)(1 − d/v) is not derived from any step I can check.

I have not verified the spatial-to-temporal transfer for the Hausdorff gauge rigorously, and I am not certain of the source result. Solution 1 is the only one whose exponents follow from a consistent chain of scaling arguments.

CHOICE: 1
